Rashi on Chullin 52b:10:1.hebrew: וכי תימא - אי לאו דרב, הוה אמינא: לעולם חתול נמי הויא דריסה בדקה, ומתניתין קא משמע לן דזאב אפילו בגסה נמי דריס, ומשום דאיירי בגסה נקט זאב:
Rashi on Chullin 52b:10:1.english: And if you would say - Were it not for Rav['s statement], I would have said: Actually, a cat also has [effective] clawing in [the case of] a small [animal], and the mishna teaches us that a wolf claws even in [the case of] a large [animal], and because it was dealing with a large [animal], it mentioned a wolf.

Rashi on Chullin 52b:12:1.hebrew: גברא אגברא קא רמית - דרבי אלעזר אדרב? דרב סבר: רבי יהודה פליג, ות"ק אפילו בגסה קאמר, ואיצטריך דרב לאשמועינן דמן הזאב ולמטה אפילו בדקה נמי לא; דלא תימא: האי דקתני זאב — משום גסה, אבל דקה אפילו חתול נמי:
Rashi on Chullin 52b:12:1.english: Are you setting one man against another man? - [The statement] of Rabbi Elazar against [that] of Rav? For Rav maintains [that] Rabbi Yehuda disagrees, and the first tanna says [that a wolf's clawing applies] even to a large [animal]. And Rav's [statement] was necessary to teach us that from a wolf and downward, even in [the case of] a small [animal, clawing does] not [apply] either; so that you should not say: That which [the Mishnah] taught, "a wolf," was on account of a large [animal], but [in the case of] a small [animal], even a cat [claws] as well.

Rashi on Chullin 52b:12:2.hebrew: ואיבעית אימא לעולם - מתניתין נמי ממעט חתול אפילו מדקה, דזאב גופיה דקתני — בדקה קאמר, כר' בנימין. ואתא רב לפרושי דדוקא נקיט זאב במתני':
Rashi on Chullin 52b:12:2.english: And if you wish, say: Actually - The Mishnah, too, excludes a cat even from a small [animal], for [regarding] a wolf itself which it taught, it stated [this] with regard to a small [animal], in accordance with Rabbi Binyamin. And Rav came to explain that [the Tanna] specifically mentioned a wolf in the Mishnah:

Rashi on Chullin 52b:12:3.hebrew: מהו דתימא - האי דנקט זאב משום דאורחיה למידרס, ולעולם הוא הדין לחתול — קמ"ל רב:
Rashi on Chullin 52b:12:3.english: Lest you say - That which [the Mishnah] mentioned a wolf is because it is its way to claw, and really the same law applies to a cat — Rav teaches us [that it is specifically a wolf].

Rashi on Chullin 52b:13:1.hebrew: נמייה - חיה היא, ויש אומרים שהיא מרטרינ"א בלע"ז:
Rashi on Chullin 52b:13:1.english: A mongoose - It is a wild animal, and some say that it is martrine [a marten] in Old French.

Rashi on Chullin 52b:13:2.hebrew: גדיים וטלאים - דקים שבדקה, ומודה רב חסדא באילים ורחלים, כמתני':
Rashi on Chullin 52b:13:2.english: Kids and lambs - [These are] the smallest among small [livestock], and Rav Ḥisda concedes regarding rams and ewes, in accordance with our Mishnah.

Rashi on Chullin 52b:13:3.hebrew: עד שתינקב לחלל - כקוץ בעלמא, ועד שניקבו הדקין. ומדשוי להו כקוץ בנקובה — מכלל דארס שלה אין מזיק אפילו לעופות, וכל שכן לגדיים וטלאים:
Rashi on Chullin 52b:13:3.english: Until it is perforated to the cavity - [Their claw is treated] like an ordinary thorn, and [it is not a tereifah] until the intestines are perforated. And since [the baraita] equated them to a thorn regarding perforation, [it follows] by implication that their venom does not cause harm even to birds, and all the more so to kids and lambs.

Rashi on Chullin 52b:15:1.english: Berebbi - The name of a sage.

Rashi on Chullin 52b:15:2.english: They did not say [that] there is no clawing - With regard to a cat.

Rashi on Chullin 52b:15:3.hebrew: אלא במקום שאין מצילין - לעוף או לגדי מידו, דאינו כועס כל כך ולא אלים זיהריה:
Rashi on Chullin 52b:15:3.english: Only in a place where there are none to rescue - [To rescue] the bird or the kid from its grasp; for it is not so angry, and its venom is not potent.

Rashi on Chullin 52b:15:4.hebrew: אבל במקום שיש לה מציל - הוא כועס, ויש לו ארס חזק, וכשמכה בצפורן משליך בה ארס. ודרב חסדא — בשיש מצילין:
Rashi on Chullin 52b:15:4.english: But in a place where it has a rescuer - It is angry and has potent venom, and when it strikes with [its] claw, it casts venom into it. And [the statement] of Rav Ḥisda [was said in a case] where there are rescuers.

Rashi on Chullin 52b:16:1.english: With its paws - [In Old French:] pelote, [meaning the pad of the paw].

Rashi on Chullin 52b:16:2.english: Five drops of blood - Venom from [its] five claws.

Rashi on Chullin 52b:17:1.english: Saving itself - In that [the hen] itself saves its body and flees.

Rashi on Chullin 52b:17:2.hebrew: ורבנן - דפליגי עליה דבריבי, דאמרי: אפילו יש מצילין אין דרוסה — בהאי דמא דמשתכח בדשא מפרקי לך:
Rashi on Chullin 52b:17:2.english: And the Rabbis - Who disagree with Berebbi, saying [that] even [where] there are rescuers there is no [effective] clawing — regarding this blood that was found on the door, they resolve [it] for you:

Rashi on Chullin 52b:17:3.english: It has venom, but it does not burn - It does not burn.

Rashi on Chullin 52b:18:1.hebrew: איכא דאמרי - דרב חסדא אפילו במקום שאין מצילין קאמר דיש דרוסה, ומתניתין דנקט זאב — משום אימרי רברבי נקט, והא מתניתין דנקט עד שתנקב לחלל — בריבי היא, ובמקום שאין מצילין, ורבנן פליגי עליה:
Rashi on Chullin 52b:18:1.english: There are those who state - That Rav Ḥisda said that there is [effective] clawing even in a place where there are no rescuers; and the Mishnah, which specified a wolf, specified [it] because of large sheep; and this teaching, which specified "until it is perforated to the cavity," is [the opinion of] Biribi, and [speaks] in [a case] where there are no rescuers, and the Rabbis disagree with him.

Rashi on Chullin 52b:18:2.english: They did not say - [that] there is clawing by a cat.

Rashi on Chullin 52b:18:3.english: But in a place where there are none to save, etc. - And the Rabbis hold that even in a place where there are none to save [it], there is clawing.

Rashi on Chullin 52b:1:1.english: How much [is considered] a deficiency in the spine - So that it does not transmit impurity in a tent without flesh.

Rashi on Chullin 52b:1:2.english: And so too with regard to a tereifa - For according to Beit Hillel, it is rendered a tereifa by one vertebra. Evidently, according to Shmuel, it is the removal of a vertebra that renders [it] a tereifa, and not the removal of a rib.

Rashi on Chullin 52b:3:1.english: At the ends of the flanks - There are many vertebrae where there are no ribs.

Rashi on Chullin 52b:4:1.hebrew: ולתנייה גבי קולי בית שמאי - אי לענין טרפה נמי פליגי, ליתנייה בעדיות, דקחשיב התם כל קולי בית שמאי וחומרי בית הלל, דהא לגבי טרפה הוו בית שמאי לקולא:
Rashi on Chullin 52b:4:1.english: And let it be taught among the leniencies of Beit Shammai - If they also disagree with regard to a tereifa, let it be taught in [tractate] Eduyyot, which enumerates there all the leniencies of Beit Shammai and the stringencies of Beit Hillel, for with regard to a tereifa, Beit Shammai are lenient.

Rashi on Chullin 52b:4:2.english: When it was asked - [The question of] a deficiency of the spine in the study hall.

Rashi on Chullin 52b:4:3.hebrew: לענין - טומאת אהל נשאלה לפניהם: בכמה חסרונה? דהתם בית שמאי לחומרא:
Rashi on Chullin 52b:4:3.english: With regard to - [Concerning] the ritual impurity of a tent it was asked before them: How much is its deficiency? For there, Beit Shammai are [the ones who rule] stringently.

Rashi on Chullin 52b:5:1.english: The majority of its height - [This is measured] from the eyes and upward. The majority of its circumference is greater than the majority of its height.

Rashi on Chullin 52b:6:1.hebrew: ברוב קרוע - וכ"ש ברוב נטולה:
Rashi on Chullin 52b:6:1.english: Where the majority is torn - And all the more so where the majority is removed.

Rashi on Chullin 52b:6:2.hebrew: או ברוב נטול - שניטל רובה, אבל ברוב קרוע לא מיטרפא:
Rashi on Chullin 52b:6:2.english: Or where the majority was removed - That its majority was removed, but in [a case where] the majority was torn, it is not rendered a tereifa.

Rashi on Chullin 52b:7:1.hebrew: תפשוט - דברוב קרוע קאמר, דהא "או שנקרע" תנן, ומפרשינן להאי רוב חיצונה דהיינו בשר החופה:
Rashi on Chullin 52b:7:1.english: Resolve [it] - That he meant [even] where the majority is torn; for behold, we learned: "Or if it was torn," and we explain this "majority of the outer [rumen]" as being the flesh that envelops [it].

Rashi on Chullin 52b:8:1.hebrew: מידי הוא טעמא - הא דמיבעיא לן: ברוב קרוע, או ברוב נטול:
Rashi on Chullin 52b:8:1.english: Is the reason anything - That which was a dilemma to us: [whether it is] where the majority is torn, or where the majority is removed.

Rashi on Chullin 52b:8:2.hebrew: אלא לשמואל - דהא איהו אמרה להא שמעתא לעיל: "צלע שנעקרה" וכו', ושמואל לא מפרש למתניתין כדאמרי במערבא, אלא מקום שאין בו מילת — דהיינו בכרס עצמו. ואיהו מוסיף האי טרפות דבשר החופה אמתניתין, דגמרא גמירי ליה, ותנא דמתניתין מייתי לה ב"זה הכלל":
Rashi on Chullin 52b:8:2.english: Only according to Shmuel - For he stated this teaching above: "A rib that was uprooted," etc., and Shmuel does not explain the Mishnah as they say in the West, but rather [as] the place that has no wool, which is in the rumen itself. And he adds this [case of] tereifa of the flesh that envelops [the rumen] to the Mishnah, for he learned it by tradition, and the Tanna of the Mishnah includes it in "This is the general rule."

Rashi on Chullin 52b:9:1.hebrew: מן הזאב ולמעלה - הוי דרוסה, וזאב בכלל. אבל מזאב ולמטה — אין לו ארס חזק להמית בהמה, אלא עופות:
Rashi on Chullin 52b:9:1.english: From a wolf and upward - It is [considered] clawing, and a wolf is included. But from [a predator smaller than] a wolf and downward, it does not have venom strong enough to kill an animal, only birds.

Rashi on Chullin 52b:9:2.english: And with regard to birds - That are clawed.

Rashi on Chullin 52b:9:3.english: From the hawk and upward - It has the strength to claw its fellow bird.

Tosafot on Chullin 52b:10:1.hebrew: אילימא למעוטי חתול - כלומר: דוקא זאב דריס באימרי רברבי, ולא חתול:
Tosafot on Chullin 52b:10:1.english: If we say to exclude a cat - That is to say, specifically a wolf claws large sheep, but not a cat.

Tosafot on Chullin 52b:10:2.hebrew: וכי תימא קמשמע לן דזאב בגסה נמי דריס - כלומר: דלהכי נקט "מן הזאב ולמעלה", לאשמועינן דכל "מן הזאב ולמעלה" שוה — דמה ארי בגסה, אף זאב בגסה:
Tosafot on Chullin 52b:10:2.english: “And if you would say: It teaches us that a wolf also claws a large [animal]” - That is to say, that for this [reason] he stated “from the wolf and upward,” to teach us that everything “from the wolf and upward” is equal — that just as a lion [claws] a large [animal], so too a wolf [claws] a large [animal].

Tosafot on Chullin 52b:13:1.hebrew: הכי גרסינן אמר רב חסדא דרוסת חתול ונמייה בגדיים וטלאים - ולא גרסינן נץ במילתיה דרב חסדא. דאי גרס ליה, א"כ כי פריך ליה מברייתא — מנץ נמי פריך; וכי משני: "הוא דאמר כבריבי", צריך לומר דקאי נמי בריבי אנץ, ואילו מתני' קתני נץ דיש לו דרוסה, ומתניתין איירי בכל ענין, אף במקום שאין מצילין! וכי תימא דמאי דמחלק בריבי היינו בגדיים וטלאים, אבל בעופות לא — א"כ מאי קא פריך מההיא תרנגולתא דהוה בי רב כהנא? ואע"פ שעל כרחך אנו צריכין לחלק משום דלא תקשה ברייתא אמתניתין, היינו משום דקסבר דבעופות קלי זיהריה ובגדיים וטלאים לא קלי זיהריה; אבל בריבי סובר דמקום שיש לו מצילין קלי בין בעופות בין בגדיים וטלאים, אבל במקום שאין מצילין אין לו כלל ארס. ואי הוה גרסינן נץ במילתא דרב חסדא, אם כן אף בנץ נמי היינו צריכין לומר כן. ועוד, לאיכא דאמרי דמשני דברייתא כבריבי היא, א"כ לרב חסדא יש דרוסה לנץ בכל ענין, אף בגדיים וטלאים; ומאי איריא דתני מתניתין עוף הדק? אפילו גדיים וטלאים נמי:
Tosafot on Chullin 52b:13:1.english: This is the version we read: "Rav Ḥisda says: The clawing of a cat or a mongoose [renders a tereifa] in kids and lambs" - And we do not read "hawk" in the statement of Rav Ḥisda. For if one were to read it, if so, when [the Gemara] raises an objection against him from the baraita, it would also object from a hawk; and when it answers: "[Rav Ḥisda] states [his opinion] in accordance with Bereibi," one would have to say that Bereibi also refers to a hawk. Whereas the Mishnah teaches that a hawk has [the ability to render a tereifa through] clawing, and our Mishnah deals with any circumstance, even in a place where there are no rescuers! And lest you say that that which Bereibi distinguishes is in [the case of] kids and lambs, but in [the case of] birds he does not — if so, what is [the Gemara's] objection from that hen that was in the house of Rav Kahana? And even though perforce we must distinguish [between birds and kids/lambs according to the baraita] so that the baraita will not contradict the Mishnah, that is because [the Tanna of the baraita] holds that in birds its venom burns, while in kids and lambs its venom does not burn; but Bereibi holds that in a place where there are rescuers [its venom] burns, both in birds and in kids and lambs, whereas in a place where there are no rescuers it has no venom at all. And had we read "hawk" in the statement of Rav Ḥisda, if so, with regard to a hawk as well we would have had to say so. And furthermore, according to the "there are those who say" who answer that the baraita is [in accordance with] Bereibi, if so, according to Rav Ḥisda a hawk has [the ability to render a tereifa through] clawing in all circumstances, even in kids and lambs; why, then, did the Mishnah specifically teach "a small bird"? Even kids and lambs as well!

Tosafot on Chullin 52b:15:1.hebrew: מ"מ לרב חסדא קשיא - וא"ת: ולישני ליה דברייתא באימרי רברבי? וי"ל: דדומיא דנץ קתני, דאף בגדיים וטלאים אין לו דרוסה. ומיהו לפירוש איכא דאמרי, דאוקי לברייתא כבריבי ובאין לו מצילין, לא הוי חתול דומיא דנץ — דדרוסת הנץ בעופות בכל ענין, ובגדיים וטלאים לא דריס בשום ענין. ומתוך כך יתיישב אמאי לא מוקי ברייתא נמי ללישנא קמא כבריבי ובאין להן מצילין — הא במצילין יש להן דרוסה — משום דדומיא דנץ קתני, דאין לו דרוסה בכל ענין:
Tosafot on Chullin 52b:15:1.english: "In any case, [it poses] a difficulty for Rav Ḥisda" - And if you say: Let [the Gemara] answer that the baraita [is dealing with] large sheep? And one can say: It teaches [the cat] similar to a hawk, [namely,] that even in kids and lambs it has no clawing. However, according to the explanation of the [version of] "there are those who say," which established the baraita in accordance with BeRebbi and [specifically in a case] where there are none to save it, a cat is not similar to a hawk — for the clawing of a hawk in birds [applies] in all circumstances, and in kids and lambs it does not claw in any circumstance. And from this, it is settled why the first version also did not establish the baraita in accordance with BeRebbi and [in a case] where they have none to save them — [which would imply that] where there are [those who] save them, they do have clawing — because it teaches [the cat] similar to a hawk, which has no clawing in any circumstance.
